newsitem.title: CHINA: Trader confirms sales of Chinese corn to Malaysia.
newsitem.headline: Trader confirms sales of Chinese corn to Malaysia.

text.p: A Chinese government grain trading company last week sold a 12,000-tonne cargo of corn to Malaysia for $152 a tonne C&F, a trader with the company who did the deal said on Friday.
Speaking on condition of anonymity, the trader said the corn was sold by a government food trading agency in northeastern Jilin for nearby shipment.
Jilin is one of China's major corn producing provinces.
The trader, speaking by telephone from China's southwestern Sichuan province, said the selling price was high and made further business difficult.

Unless the FOB (free on board) price of corn loading at China's northern port of Dalian fell from its current level of around 1,100 yuan ($132.50) a tonne, he said he was unlikely to be able to sell more Chinese corn into the regional market.

Far East traders have said Chinese corn sales into the region so far this month could reach 300,000 tonnes by the close of business Friday. They were awaiting confirmation of a 145,000-tonne government-to-government deal to the Philippines.
A Singapore trading source said Chinese corn sales to Malaysia this month had already topped 40,000 tonnes, all for February/March delivery and all sold at around $151-152 a tonne.
Corn futures in Chicago were lower on Thursday on reports of Chinese corn sales, among the first major shipments since a ban was imposed on corn exports in December 1994.
China last week sold 76,000 tonnes to South Korea.
Japanese traders have said they would be willing to buy Chinese corn if the price is right and if exports are given the official go-ahead.
